title: lifedraft input contract — universal $defs: the trading_friction block
$comment: Fragment of the universal input contract, merged into schema/input_schema.json by input_contract.load_universal_schema() -- see that function and compose_schema() for the exact, total merge rule. This file is a FRAGMENT, not a standalone schema: its "#/$defs/..." references resolve only in the composed document. Issue #143: the DECLARABLE per-transaction trading friction -- bid/ask spread and commission on the dollars the engine turns over. The engine moves money at pot level (aggregate balances), never per ticket, so the honest spelling is a proportional cost per dollar turned over (rebalance_bps) plus a flat fee only where the engine counts real events (the single year-0 lump deployment). Optional and deliberately NOT in the spine's required list (DP#16: auto-include on trigger data) -- a document that omits trading_friction trades frictionlessly, exactly as every pre-#143 run did, and the golden invariant does not move (DP#32).

rebalance_bps.description: Issue #143. The proportional cost of turning one dollar of the portfolio over, in BASIS POINTS: 5 bps on a $100,000 deployment = $50. Covers the bid/ask spread crossed on each round trip plus any ad-valorem commission; for liquid broad-market ETFs a few bps is typical, but the value is the household's DECLARED fact about its venue, not an engine assumption. Charged at each trade event the engine performs: the year-0 borrowed lump deployment and each year's savings deployment into the pots. A declared 0 is valid and distinct from omitting the block (DP#32: zero is a value, not a fallback); a negative value is refused at load.

per_trade_fee.description: Issue #143. A FLAT commission charged per COUNTED trade event (a $9.95 ticket charge), not per dollar. Deliberately narrow: the engine moves money at aggregate-pot level and cannot observe how many tickets a real account traded, so this fee is priced ONLY at the one seam where the event count is honest -- the year-0 lump deployment, which crosses through exactly one allocation call. Omit (or declare 0) when the venue is genuinely zero-commission or when only the spread matters.
